hints.title: Single Child Depth Obstacle
hints.text: If a node has only one child, can taking the minimum of child depths incorrectly count the missing child with depth 0? How does finding the first leaf node in a tier-by-tier traversal avoid traversing deeper branches?

hints.title: First Leaf Level Invariant
hints.text: The minimum depth is the distance to the very first leaf node encountered. Processing nodes tier by tier guarantees that the first leaf reached yields the minimum depth immediately.

hints.title: Tier-by-Tier Early Return Procedure
hints.text: If root is null, return 0. Use a queue initialized with root and track depth starting at 1. For each level, pop nodes; if a node has neither left nor right child, return current depth immediately. Otherwise, enqueue its non-null children and increment depth per tier.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (0 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Early-exit breadth-first search stopping immediately upon encountering the shallowest leaf node.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Blindly returning min(left, right) + 1 when a node has only one child incorrectly treats null as a leaf of depth 0.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: BFS requires O(W) auxiliary space but visits strictly fewer nodes than full DFS on skewed trees.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct handling of nodes with only one child and early termination on the first leaf.
